title: Agent API: add `duration` to the named params - every agent video runs the workflow default
description:
`POST /connector/generate` has no `duration` named param, so an agent cannot ask for a
video length. `routes/connector.js:411`:

    const NAMED_PARAM_KEYS = ['ratio', 'qualityTier', 'turbo', 'styleSelect', 'stylization'];

Every agent-dispatched video therefore runs whatever `Input_Duration` the workflow file
bakes in. For H3 that is 2, which snaps to 56 frames / 2.33 s - BELOW the 124-362 trained
range recorded in `docs/models/h3/README.md`. The in-app agent (MPI-774) and an external
agent driving the app through the cubric-vision skill both submit through this one route,
so both are affected.

Evidence (user's own projects, 2026-09-19): all three `fanvue/ref2v_*` sidecars carry NO
`Input_Duration` in `injectionParams` and landed at 56 frames while `controlState.shared.duration`
says 5. Every clip made through the UI in the other projects carries the key.

There IS an escape hatch already - raw `injectionParams: { Input_Duration: 5 }` passes
straight through (`routes/connector.js:487`) - but it needs the agent to know the node
title, so the friendly layer silently disagrees with the app's own slider.

Scope:
- add `duration` to `NAMED_PARAM_KEYS` and to the resolver in `js/data/generationControls.js`
  (DOM-free, used by both the route's static validation and `js/shell/agentDispatch.js`)
- it is a per-model concern: H3 snaps to a 17k+5 frame grid, other video models do not,
  so the resolver should report back what the run will ACTUALLY get, as `MpiH3Length` does
- decide whether an out-of-trained-range ask warns (H3: below 124 frames)
- update the cubric-vision-generate skill so agents reach for the named param, not the raw node

Found while investigating a period-4 duplicate-frame artefact in H3 ref2v output. That
artefact is a separate, model-side issue and is NOT this card.
